# Certified auxiliary counterexamples

## Half-depth integer rounding fails (depth/Helly agent)

Let d >= 2, and let K be a d-simplex with centroid 0. Define
C = conv(({0} x K) union ({1} x (-K))) in R x R^d.
This is a full-dimensional convex body. Its mixed-integer intersection is
S = ({0} x K) union ({1} x (-K)), and both fibers have equal volume.

The unrestricted point c = (1/2, 0) has normalized halfspace depth 1/2:
central reflection through c preserves S and its measure, so every closed
halfspace containing c has at least half the mass. Some hyperplanes through c
have zero boundary mass, so the depth is exactly 1/2.

For any y in either fiber and any halfspace cap G through its continuous
coordinate, an ambient halfspace through y with sufficiently large integer
normal can realize G on that fiber and exclude the other fiber completely.
The largest halfspace depth inside a simplex is gamma_d. Consequently
max_{y in S} depth_S(y) <= gamma_d / 2. Equality holds at either fiber
centroid, because every ambient halfspace containing it has at least a
gamma_d fraction of that fiber's mass. Hence restricting one real coordinate
to an integer coordinate can reduce the optimal depth by exactly gamma_d,
which is strictly less than 1/2 for d >= 2. This disproves a general induction
lemma that claims integer rounding loses at most a factor 1/2 of an existing
continuous halfspace-depth guarantee.

## Fiber-centroid restriction fails in n=1, d=2 (depth/Helly agent)

Let T = {(x,y): x >= 0, y >= 0, x+y <= 1}. Its area is 1/2 and its
centroid is g=(1/3,1/3). Let B = T intersect {x <= 1/3}.
The cap T intersect {x >= 1/3} has area (2/3)^2 area(T) = 4 area(T)/9,
so area(B)=5 area(T)/9. Define
C = conv(({-1} x B) union ({0} x T) union ({1} x B)).
Its integer fibers are exactly B,T,B, and it is a full-dimensional convex
body. Their total mass is (19/9) area(T).

At the middle fiber centroid (0,g), the halfspace {x >= 1/3} captures
4 area(T)/9 and zero area from the endpoint fibers. Its normalized mass is
4/19 < 2/9 = 2^{-1} gamma_2.

At either endpoint fiber centroid, take any continuous halfspace through the
centroid with at most half of B's area (one of two complementary halfspaces
always does), and tilt in the integer coordinate sufficiently to exclude the
other two fibers. This captures at most area(B)/2, a normalized mass of
5/38 < 2/9. Therefore none of the three fiber centroids achieves OC.

All assertions are exact; the displayed caps have boundaries carrying zero
2-dimensional fiber measure. This does not refute OC: a suitable noncentroid
point in the middle fiber may still satisfy its required bound.

## Weighted-median midpoint fails in n=d=1 (depth/Helly agent)

Let C=conv{(-1,0),(3,0),(0,5),(-1,2)}. Fiber lengths at integer
coordinates -1,0,1,2,3 are 2,5,10/3,5/3,0; total length is 12.
The unique weighted median fiber is k=0. The cap t >= k/2 + 5/2
through its midpoint (0,5/2) has mass 5/2+1/3=17/6, hence normalized
mass 17/72 < 1/4. This falsifies selection of a weighted-median fiber
followed by its centroid even in the smallest mixed dimension.

## Every fiber midpoint fails in n=d=1 (depth/Helly agent)

Let C=conv{(0,0),(3,0),(3,3),(2,10),(0,2)}. This is a full-dimensional
integer pentagon in R^2. Its four integer fibers at k=0,1,2,3 are respectively
[0,2], [0,6], [0,10], [0,3]. Their total 1-dimensional Hausdorff measure is
21, so the required OC cap mass is 21/4.

The four fiber midpoints and respective certifying closed caps are:

* (0,1): t >= 11k+1; captured fiber lengths are 1,0,0,0.
* (1,3): t >= 11(k-1)+3; captured lengths are 2,3,0,0, total 5.
* (2,5): t >= 9-2k; captured lengths are 0,0,5,0.
* (3,3/2): t >= -11(k-3)+3/2; captured lengths are 0,0,0,3/2.

Every displayed cap contains its candidate midpoint on the boundary. The
captured mass is at most 5 < 21/4, so every fiber centroid fails OC. This
refutes the existential centroid restriction, not merely a particular choice
of integer fiber. All coordinates and cap normals are rational, all mass
calculations are exact, and cap boundaries carry zero relevant measure.

## Marginal-depth lifting fails for n=1, d=4 (depth/Helly agent)

The proposed implication was: if an integer base point z has normalized
halfspace depth beta for the fiber-volume marginal nu, then some point of its
fiber has normalized ambient depth at least gamma_d beta. The following
counterexample disproves that implication.

Let T be the standard 4-simplex, with barycentric coordinates lambda_0,...,
lambda_4, and write V=vol_4(T). Put r=1/10, epsilon=r^4=1/10000, and
B={x in T: lambda_0(x)>=1-r}. Thus vol_4(B)=epsilon V and, on B,
lambda_i<=r for i=1,...,4. Define
C=conv(({-1} x B) union ({0} x T) union ({1} x B)).
Its integer fibers are exactly B,T,B and total mass is (1+2 epsilon)V.
The marginal point z=0 has depth beta=(1+epsilon)/(1+2 epsilon).

Let gamma_4=256/625 and t=gamma_4(1+epsilon)=160016/390625.
If a point (0,x) had the proposed normalized depth gamma_4 beta, every
halfspace containing it would have unnormalized mass at least t V.
Write lambda_i=lambda_i(x). The vertex cap lambda_i(w)>=lambda_i has
T-volume (1-lambda_i)^4 V.

For i=1,...,4, if lambda_i>r this cap meets neither endpoint fiber in positive
measure, and hence its required mass implies lambda_i<=1-t^(1/4).
If lambda_i<=r, the same conclusion holds automatically because
r<1-t^(1/4), as t<(9/10)^4. For i=0, its endpoint-fiber contribution is at
most 2 epsilon V, so the required mass implies
lambda_0<=1-(t-2 epsilon)^(1/4).

These five inequalities contradict sum_i lambda_i=1. Indeed the following
are exact rational certificates:

a=8000199/10000000,
b=7999223/10000000,
t-a^4=2032792963819263760799/10^28 > 0,
t-2 epsilon-b^4=664183074753367294559/10^28 > 0,
4a+b-4=19/10000000 > 0.

Thus 4 t^(1/4)+(t-2 epsilon)^(1/4)>4, and summing the five bounds gives
sum_i lambda_i < 5-4 = 1. No point of the integer fiber z=0 achieves the
claimed lifting guarantee. C is a full-dimensional convex body, and all
measures here are ordinary full-dimensional mixed-integer fiber volumes.

This does not contradict OC; the disproved guarantee is stronger and uses
the high marginal depth beta, which here is close to 1. The mathematical
mechanism is that d+1 vertex caps must share the adjustment caused by the two
small endpoint fibers. The same construction works for all d with
(d+1) gamma_d>2, in particular every d>=4, for sufficiently small r.
